paragraphs: One-line judgment｜Only if you are willing to make judgments in high-risk, highly uncertain obstetric and gynecological settings, take on surgical and medication decisions, keep up continuous communication with patients and the team, and accept long-term medical education and licensure requirements, is this occupation worth continuing to explore; being drawn only to the image of helping mothers and babies is not enough.

Core output｜Linking history and examination, diagnosis and differential diagnosis, treatment and medication, surgical records, and follow-up and referral into a traceable clinical record: reviewable clinical decisions and patient outcomes, not a single consultation action.

20—120 minute safe trial｜Use a fictional case for one off-site exercise: based on the given hypertensive-disorders-of-pregnancy scenario excerpt, write three critical signs requiring immediate assessment, two bases for judgment that prompt referral or consultation, and a clinical record covering examination, medication, and follow-up points. The exercise uses fictional data only, and no diagnosis, treatment, or surgery may be performed on any real patient.

First threshold｜First confirm the qualification and authorization boundaries: who holds a license to practice, who may prescribe and perform surgery, and who bears responsibility when critical signs appear. In the United States, medical school education and residency training must be completed and a state license obtained; in mainland China, a licensed physician qualification must be obtained and registration completed, and providing services such as midwifery techniques also requires a maternal and child health technical service license.

entries: Pregnancy and childbirth care｜Providing prenatal examination, childbirth, and postpartum care, and identifying and managing pregnancy complications and critical signs.
Gynecological disease diagnosis and treatment｜Diagnosing and treating menstrual disorders, infections, tumors, and reproductive system diseases, and providing prevention and health advice.
Surgery and procedures｜Performing or taking part in obstetric and gynecological surgery and procedures, and completing pre- and post-operative risk assessment, informed communication, and follow-up.
Medication and treatment decisions｜Writing prescriptions and non-intravenous administration, setting treatment plans, and monitoring efficacy and adverse reactions.
Examination and interpretation｜Collecting history and examination data, and interpreting laboratory and imaging results to support diagnosis and management.
Collaboration, referral, and teaching｜Collaborating with other professionals, referring cases beyond scope, and supervising patient care staff and teaching work.

paragraphs: Obstetricians and gynecologists (O*NET-SOC 29-1218.00, Obstetricians and Gynecologists) provide medical care related to pregnancy and childbirth, diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases of women, especially those affecting the reproductive system; they may also provide general care for women and take on medical and gynecological surgical functions. This page uses only official sources to explain occupational scope, tasks, China-U.S. access differences, and statistical measures.

Work settings are mainly hospital obstetric units, gynecology clinics, and operating rooms; O*NET shows 98% in contact with others continuously, 100% holding face-to-face discussions daily, 100% working in a controlled indoor environment daily, 93% communicating by telephone daily, 86% having a great deal of decision freedom, 89% considering teamwork extremely important, 84% considering accuracy extremely important, 79% wearing routine protective equipment daily, 71% exposed to disease or infection daily, 62% considering the consequences of error extremely serious, 88% with a regular schedule, and 67% working more than 40 hours per week.

Typical inputs are history and examination data, laboratory and imaging results, patient preferences, and past history; typical outputs are traceable clinical decisions, surgical and medication records, and follow-up and referral arrangements. Key judgments include whether emergency intervention is needed, whether conservative treatment can continue, when to refer or consult, and whether the record supports review by others.

O*NET's interest code is ISR (Investigative, Social, Realistic); Job Zone 5 (SVP 8.0 and above), where most posts require medical school education and long-term clinical training; the skill focus centers on critical thinking, reading comprehension, active learning, active listening, monitoring, speaking, and writing, and requires scientific literacy. These dimensions describe activity preferences and job requirements and must not be treated as hiring criteria, competence assessment conclusions, or judgments about career destiny.

Scope of responsibility｜In the United States, a license to practice must be obtained in the state concerned; medical school education, specialty residency training, and examination requirements are verified with the state medical board. Specialty certification may affect recruitment and institutional authorization but is not a uniform statutory prerequisite for all physicians in independent practice. In mainland China, physician qualification must be obtained and practice registration completed; special technical services such as midwifery and termination of pregnancy also require verifying the institution's service license and the staff's passing certificate or the technical category endorsement on the practice certificate.

The competence focus is making reviewable clinical decisions under time pressure: being able to map history, examination, and patient preferences to diagnosis, treatment plan, and referral criteria; standards of documentation and communication must be maintained amid high-frequency decisions, exposure, and conflict situations.

This page does not treat interest codes or work styles as a practitioner profile: ISR describes only activity preferences, and practice competence must still be verified through training records, licensure, peer evaluation, and real case outcomes.

Obstetricians and gynecologists are adjacent to midwives, physician assistants, registered nurses, family medicine and general internal medicine physicians, anesthesiologists, and pediatricians, and should be distinguished by primary work object, independent practice and prescribing authority, surgical and obstetric authorization, and scope of responsibility, not by similarity of job titles.

The comparison objects in this table come from the official tasks and adjacent occupation descriptions of O*NET 29-1218.00 and from China-U.S. practice and authorization systems; obstetricians and gynecologists are independent specialist physicians in the United States, while in mainland China a licensed physician qualification must be obtained and techniques such as midwifery performed within the scope of the maternal and child health technical service license.

The table below compares this occupation with adjacent directions along the same dimensions: primary work object, core output, key differences, and selection signals; the comparison is for career exploration and does not represent mutual recognition of qualifications, automatic job transfer, or a hiring promise.

Midwives mainly provide continuity of maternal care and management of low-risk labor, referring surgery and high-risk situations onward; physician assistants take part in diagnosis and treatment and prescribing under supervision or collaboration; registered nurses are responsible for nursing assessment and carrying out physician orders; family medicine and general internal medicine physicians provide general practice but usually do not perform obstetric surgery; anesthesiologists are responsible for anesthesia and perioperative management; pediatricians work with children and adolescents. The core difference for obstetricians and gynecologists is independently taking on the diagnosis, treatment, and surgical decisions for pregnancy and gynecological diseases.

If you want to make independent diagnostic, medication, and surgical decisions and bear long-term responsibility in maternal and women's health, continue exploring this occupation; if you want a shorter training period or a focus on continuity of care, nursing, anesthesia, or pediatrics, compare the corresponding directions and verify licensure and authorization requirements.
Clinical staff who want to start with digital tools

First practice medical record writing, examination interpretation, and treatment outlines with public textbooks and simulated scenarios; treat tools as learning and review assistants and do not use them to replace diagnosis, prescribing, or surgical decisions.
Practicing obstetricians and gynecologists

Use tools for medical record summaries and drafts organizing examination results; keep raw examination data and the basis for judgment, and anything entering the formal medical record must be reviewed by a person and signed.
Department and medical quality managers

Clarify which tool outputs may enter medical and quality control records and which must be reviewed by a person; archive according to medical institution policy and adverse event reporting requirements.
People transitioning in from other fields

People transferring into this field in mainland China must first obtain licensed physician qualification and complete registration, and providing midwifery techniques also requires a special license; in the United States medical school education and residency training must be completed and a state license obtained; other professional backgrounds cannot directly substitute for these requirements.

Name and scope｜This occupation corresponds to O*NET-SOC 29-1218.00 (Obstetricians and Gynecologists). The corresponding occupation in mainland China is the obstetrician-gynecologist, who must obtain licensed physician qualification and complete practice registration, and must also obtain the corresponding license to provide maternal and child health technical services such as midwifery techniques and termination of pregnancy.

Measure comparison｜The sources checked this time did not obtain a precise national wage for obstetricians and gynecologists: the MOHRSS enterprise pay survey publishes wage levels for health professional technical personnel by occupational mid-category, and the National Bureau of Statistics publishes average wages for health and social work by industry sector; this page uses these two proxy measures for reference and marks their boundaries separately.

Verifiable reference｜The MOHRSS 2024 enterprise pay survey shows a median wage level of 6.36 ten-thousand yuan/year for health professional technical personnel, with the 10%—90% percentile at 3.50—14.51 ten-thousand yuan/year; the National Bureau of Statistics 2025 average annual wage for the health and social work industry was 146,266 yuan for urban non-private units and 75,631 yuan for private units.

Evidence insufficient: the sources checked this time did not obtain the occupational wage distribution corresponding to obstetricians and gynecologists (O*NET 29-1218.00 Obstetricians and Gynecologists); this page shows only occupational mid-category and industry sector proxy values with their boundaries marked, and does not infer this occupation's median, percentiles, or personal income from them.

The 2025 BLS OEWS shown by O*NET gives a median annual wage of 292,910 USD and a median hourly wage of 140.82 USD for the precise occupation 29-1218.00; this measure is not a starting salary or a personal quote.
This figure is the statistical position of the national median annual wage, not a starting salary, a personal quote, or a personal income promise.

The 25th—75th percentile is 179,810—369,390 USD and the 10th—90th percentile is 94,680—437,300 USD, both from the 2025 BLS OEWS national survey, and cannot be compared directly with the pay terms of a single institution or a single shift.
The two ends of the distribution reflect spread: a low percentile is not a new-graduate starting salary, and a high percentile does not represent the general level of practitioners.

OEWS is a survey of institutional wage and salary employees, excludes self-employment income, and does not reflect differences in on-call duty, overtime, and benefits; the actual income of obstetricians and gynecologists must be verified by practice form, region, institution type, on-call duty, and obstetric workload.

U.S. figures cannot be converted into mainland China personal income, and percentile ranges cannot be read as a job-level ladder; for mainland China there are only occupational mid-category and industry sector proxy values.

paragraphs: The key signals of fit for this occupation are: maintaining diagnosis, treatment, and documentation standards in high-accuracy, high-consequence settings; making reviewable decisions under time pressure; communicating continuously with patients and the team; and being willing to keep updating medical knowledge over the long term; interest and work style labels cannot determine fit.

The interest code and work styles come from the O*NET 29-1218.00 summary and are exploratory evidence; the fit signals and trial design on this page are editorial synthesis and do not constitute selection criteria, competence assessment, or a hiring promise.

Boundary statement｜This checklist cannot replace medical institutions' diagnostic and treatment standards, prescribing and surgical authorization systems, infection control systems, or adverse event reporting systems. The main risks center on: delayed recognition and referral of critical signs, medication and surgical verification errors, infection and body fluid exposure, poor maternal and neonatal outcomes, and missing documentation and informed communication; control requirements should be tailored to institutional authorization and local rules.

Direct answer｜The main risks of this occupation are failure to identify and escalate critical signs in time, missed diagnosis and differential diagnosis, medication and surgical verification errors, inadequate infection exposure protection, and missing documentation and informed communication; control depends on structured assessment, critical value and adverse event reporting systems, two-person verification, and post-exposure management.

Evidence scope｜The risk items come from the work context of O*NET 29-1218.00 (62% considering the consequences of error extremely serious, 84% considering accuracy extremely important, 71% exposed to disease or infection daily, 75% working very close to others, 67% working more than 40 hours per week) and its official tasks, together with mainland China's licensed physician and maternal and child health technical service licensing systems.

Affected roles｜Physicians who take on obstetric and gynecological diagnosis and treatment, medication, and surgery, together with collaborating midwifery, anesthesia, nursing, and neonatal teams. The editorial recommendation focuses on verification and documentation during night shifts, high load, and handover periods; no data comparing omission probability by period was obtained here.

Possible consequences｜Delayed critical signs affect the safety of the mother and fetus; medication or surgical verification errors cause direct harm; inadequate infection exposure protection harms occupational health; missing documentation and informed communication affects accountability and patient trust.

Recruitment sample (editorial compilation)｜This page does not copy any single employer's recruitment notice; the following are post sample points compiled from O*NET tasks, industry requirements, and China-U.S. systems, to help understand actual job requirements, and do not represent a current vacancy. U.S. posts usually require completed medical school education and obstetrics and gynecology residency training plus a state license to practice; mainland China posts usually require licensed physician qualification and completed registration, and providing midwifery techniques also requires a maternal and child health technical service license.

Recruitment signals: scope judgment / able to explain the responsibility and authorization boundaries between obstetricians and gynecologists, midwives, registered nurses, and family medicine physicians; work sample / able to deliver reviewable records related to history and examination, diagnosis and differential diagnosis, medication, and follow-up; risk awareness / able to recognize critical signs, infection exposure, and verification failure conditions and escalate per procedure; communication / able to hand over accurately with patients, families, and the team.

Suggested sample: complete the obstetrician-gynecologist input checklist (history and examination data, patient preferences), procedure record (diagnosis and treatment, medication and procedures), quality check (critical values, infection control, and surgical safety checkpoints), and abnormality escalation form using fictional scenarios. Real patient information must not be used.

Education and training path｜In the United States, medical school education and obstetrics and gynecology residency training are completed first, and a license to practice is obtained according to state requirements; specialty certification and institutional clinical authorization are verified separately and cannot be treated as a uniform statutory license. In mainland China, medical education, the physician qualification examination, and registration must be verified; maternal and child health special services require separate verification of institutional licensing and staff technical assessment.

Portfolio and trial｜Use fictional cases only: one page of a history and examination outline, one page of a diagnosis and differential diagnosis checklist, one page of a medication and follow-up plan, with sources, assumptions, privacy, and authorization boundaries clearly labeled.

Competence progression｜Start from the supervised resident stage, gradually take on independent clinics and obstetric on-call duty, then complex cases and lead surgery, and finally move into preceptorship, quality improvement, and specialty direction development.

Documentation and review｜The clinical record must support review by others: keep raw examination data, the basis for judgment, informed patient communication, and a responsible signature, and retain them per institutional policy.

Practice boundaries｜Licensure, prescribing authority, surgical and midwifery authorization, and institutional post authorization must be verified separately; no single qualification automatically confers clinical authority beyond the licensed scope.

Competence progression should start with supervised residency training, take on independent clinics and obstetric on-call duty after completing specialty training and obtaining licensure, then handle complex cases and surgery, and finally move into preceptorship, quality improvement, and specialty direction development; each step is premised on training assessment, licensure, and institutional authorization.

locale_requirements.credential_boundary: Academic qualifications, licensure, specialty certification, and institutional post authorization are different statuses, and no single qualification automatically confers diagnostic and treatment authority, medication authority, or surgical authority beyond the licensed scope.
locale_requirements.jurisdiction: In the United States, state medical boards and specialty certification bodies decide licensure and certification, and medical institutions decide post authorization; in mainland China, the health commission handles the physician qualification examination and practice registration, and the maternal and child health technical service license is processed separately.
locale_requirements.summary: U.S. physicians must hold a state license to practice; obstetrics and gynecology residency training, specialty certification, and institutional clinical authority are verified separately, and specialty certification is not a uniform statutory prerequisite for all physicians. In mainland China, physician qualification must be obtained and registered; midwifery and termination of pregnancy also require verifying the institution's special service license and the staff's technical assessment qualification.

facts.display_value: Obstetricians and gynecologists are distinguished from midwives, physician assistants, registered nurses, family medicine and general internal medicine physicians, anesthesiologists, and pediatricians by primary work object, independent practice, and surgical authorization, not by similarity of job titles.

In the United States, medical school education and obstetrics and gynecology residency training must be completed, specialty certification obtained, and a state license to practice acquired; in mainland China, licensed physician qualification and completed registration are required, and providing maternal and child health technical services such as midwifery techniques and termination of pregnancy also requires the corresponding license.
facts.period: The Physicians Law took effect on 2022-03-01; accessed 2026-09-26

facts.display_value: Observable fit signals: able to take on diagnostic, medication, and surgical decisions in pregnancy and gynecological settings, maintain verification and documentation habits in high-accuracy, high-consequence settings, and be willing to keep updating medical knowledge and communicate continuously.

Obstetricians and gynecologists correspond to O*NET 29-1218.00 (Obstetricians and Gynecologists): they provide medical care related to pregnancy and childbirth, diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases of women, especially those affecting the reproductive system; they may also provide general care for women and take on obstetric and gynecological surgery.
Clinical workflow: from history and examination, interpretation and differential diagnosis, treatment and medication, surgery and follow-up, to referral and documentation, forming a traceable loop.

Risk control: recognition and escalation of critical signs, two-person verification, infection control and post-exposure management, informed communication, and record archiving, tailored to institutional authorization and local rules.
Pregnancy and childbirth care, gynecological disease diagnosis and treatment, medication and surgical decisions, examination interpretation, and documentation and collaborative referral

Traceable clinical decisions: history and examination records, diagnosis and differential diagnosis, treatment and medication, surgery and follow-up records, and referral and informed communication records
